Entra ID
Foundry (Wall 0)
APIM gateway (Wall 1)
MCP servers (Wall 2)
Data plane (Wall 3)
Public edge: reachable from the Internet
Operator and control plane
Governance
Observability and audit
Closed
Soft spot
Role: five personas, the operator, the
Demo Console and test clients. Each
holds an Entra token: T1 for Foundry,
T2a for an MCP API.
Blast radius: a stolen token carries
only that person's roles.
Closed: a call with no valid token is
refused at the gateway (401). /legacy
takes a shared key instead, by design.
Soft spot: a token stays valid until it
expires (60-90 min).
Role: signs every token. App roles on
users and group membership decide
what each wall allows. Federated
credentials let the research, wall,
actions and private UAMIs ask for
OBO tokens.
Blast radius: a wrong role or group
here is inherited by every wall below.
Closed: a person with no app role (Ian)
is refused on every tool call at the
gateway and sees no tools. Nobody
holds Wall.Orion.
Soft spot: Conditional Access is
report-only. A role change can take up
to about 30 s to reach a new token.
Role: agents call only the tools in
allowed_tools. Foundry holds each
user's OAuth token per connection.
The governed agent asks a human to
approve place_order. The guardrail
screens prompts, completions and tool
output.
Blast radius: a prompt-injected agent
acts only with the caller's own token
and roles, inside allowed_tools.
Closed: tools outside allowed_tools
are not offered. place_order waits for a
human approval.
Soft spot: the guardrail is preview and
best-effort. Foundry reuses a token
until it expires, so a role change
reaches the agent late.
Role: validates the token, then refuses
a revoked user, a client not on the
allow-list, a missing scope or a missing
role. Rate limit: 120 calls per 60 s per
user.
Blast radius: if APIM is bypassed,
research, wall, actions and private
re-check the token themselves; vendor
and legacy do not. /legacy has no
token check.
Closed: 401 (token), 403 (revoked,
client, scope, role) or 429 (rate), all
before any MCP server runs.
Soft spot: the kill switch and allow-list
take 45-90 s. The private MCP server
is not behind APIM: no kill switch, no
rate limit.
Role: internal Container Apps
environment in the VNet. Re-verifies
the token, filters tools by role, then
swaps the token (OBO, with its T3
assertion) for the user's own T4a/b/c.
One UAMI per server.
Blast radius: its UAMI (audit append
and image pull; actions also reads the
restricted list; vendor reads one Key
Vault secret) plus the user tokens it is
handling. Legacy is deliberately broad.
Closed: refuses a bad token (401) or a
missing scope (403). A tool the caller
has no role for, a project not in the
token roles or an OBO failure gets a
DENIED result (HTTP 200). All are
logged.
Soft spot: the audit blob write is
asynchronous and best-effort. Search
and Cosmos logs are matched by
time.
Role: Storage, Cosmos and Search
accept private traffic only, with no
keys. The data plane's own roles are
checked on the user's own T4a/b/c
token.
Blast radius: what that person's groups
grant, and no more. Exception: actions
reads the restricted list as the service.
Closed: no data-plane role, no data.
Storage answers 403 and the server
reports storage_rbac_denied. Nobody
holds a role on wall-orion.
Soft spot: the Search role is
index-wide; public and wall documents
are split by a server-side filter.
Role: the APIM gateway (a user token, or the subscription key on
/legacy), the Foundry endpoint (keyless, Entra only), Container
Registry (admin off, pull needs AcrPull), Key Vault (default-Deny; the
NAT IP and trusted Azure services allowed) and the vendor mock (a
public Container Apps environment).
Blast radius: Storage, Cosmos and Search have no public path, and
the five internal MCP servers are reachable only from the VNet. The
vendor mock is public and protected by one static key.
Closed: APIM refuses a call with no valid token or key. The vendor
mock refuses a wrong key (401 invalid_vendor_key). Key Vault
refuses other networks.
Soft spot: the Foundry endpoint and the Container Registry stay
public (Entra-only). The vendor key is a static secret.
Role: the operator holds control-plane roles and the same data app
roles as Wes and Tara. The kill-switch and allow-list scripts write
APIM named values; Reset demo also writes group membership and
the operator's roles in Entra.
Blast radius: the operator can change the kill switch, the allow-list, the
front-door limits and their own roles. The Demo Console listens on
127.0.0.1 only; the jump box has no public IP.
Closed: the Demo Console refuses cross-origin POSTs and other
host names. No token, password or TOTP seed reaches the browser.
Soft spot: each persona's refresh token is cached in .secrets on the
operator's machine. The jump box gets one only with
-IncludePersonaFiles.
Role: Azure Policy initiative abw-agent-platform-controls (no keys,
private networking, approved tools and models, guardrails, hygiene)
and a budget with alerts at 50, 80 and 100 % actual and 100 %
forecast.
Blast radius: exemptions mark the deliberate gaps: six in all, and the
legacy keyed connection has a time-boxed waiver.
Closed: Deny stops a keyed Foundry connection, and an MCP target
outside the four APIM paths and the private server, when it is
created.
Soft spot: the budget is an alert, not a cap. The Foundry data-plane
policies are preview and report compliance only.
Role: container logs and App Insights feed Log Analytics
(AbwMcpAudit, AbwGateway, AbwFullChain). Five MCP servers also
append JSON lines to a WORM audit blob. Sentinel rules and a
workbook sit on top.
Blast radius: the logs hold user ids, tool names and a SHA-256 of the
arguments, never the arguments themselves.
Closed: nothing here refuses a call; logs and alerts only record and
notify.
Soft spot: logs arrive 2-18 min late. The audit blob is best-effort and
unlocked (1-day immutability, a demo pattern). Sentinel receives no
Entra sign-in data in this build.

Trust boundaries and failure modes
What each boundary protects, what fails closed or soft, and where to look when it breaks

One governed request crosses these boundaries in order. Each wall decides again on its own.
Around the request path: the public edge, the operator, governance and logging
Failure, symptom and where to look
The agent shows (none) for the wall, actions or private tools (or 403 on
vendor) long after the roles were fixed. Foundry keeps the token 60-90 min
and the tool list about 15-20 min.
The tool list the agent run reports ([tools/list] wall: (none)). A consent link lives
about 10 min and must be opened signed in as that persona.
Apply the persona role baseline first. Then delete the connection through ARM, run foundry-connections.ps1
-Only <name>, consent again and republish with create_agents.py --rai abw-agent-guardrails. A redirect-URI
mismatch needs foundry-connections.ps1 -Force.
401 with {error: unauthorized, server, reason} and a WWW-Authenticate
resource_metadata header.
The reason in the response body. KQL AbwGateway lists the call as Outcome
unauthenticated: a 401 never reaches the policy trace.
Right after abw-kill or abw-allow the old token no longer matches the gateway: wait about 50 s, request a new
token (abw-gw does), then run abw-kill -Reset and abw-allow -Reset.
The first call after idle takes 10-20 s.
The Container Apps replica count: it should stay at the minimum of 1.
Run abw-warm before the demo (30-60 s; it warms the gateway, every MCP replica and Foundry). Keep
minimum replicas at 1.
The tool answers FORBIDDEN obo_failed:<code>.
KQL AbwMcpAudit (event tool_denied, reason obo_failed:<code>). The UAMI
and its federated credential on the API app.
Fix what the code names. Federated credentials come from Setup-Entra.ps1 phase 2; consent to the data
resources comes from phase 1.
The red-team run just completes: the guardrail did not intervene.
Expected: the guardrail is a preview, best-effort control. When it does fire, KQL
AbwDenials shows Layer 0-agent-guardrail and Sentinel raises ABW-008.
Ask again, or show the stored blocked trace and the ABW-008 incident. Never present it as deterministic; the
wall is the control.
An Act 6 board says it is no longer in memory, or a watchtower row says
Waiting.
Boards live in the console's memory only: a restart, or newer runs, push them out.
Or the log has not arrived yet. The probe cache lasts 120 s.
Run the scenario again. Press Refresh from logs 15-20 min after the click (Entra's own sign-in log can take that
long).
HTTP 429 right after the burst beat.
The limit is 120 calls per 60 s per user. KQL AbwGateway lists the call as
Outcome rate_limited.
Wait 60 s.
An agent beat is refused with 403 token_quota_exceeded or 429
rate_limited.
The Agent entry light says not the baseline. A limit lowered by Act 7 beat 7.4 is
still in force, or the rate limiter's lock-out (about 2 min) is still counting down.
Reset demo puts both settings back (APIM named values abw-agent-token-quota and abw-agent-rpm) and waits
until the front door forwards.
abw-chain returns 0 rows or only the gateway row. A Sentinel incident has
not appeared.
Ingestion lag of 5-10 min (the MCP-server row of a denial can take longer), or the
wrong request id. Sentinel incidents appear up to about 8 min after the event
(about 13 for ABW-007).
Wait, then run it again. For abw-chain -Allowed, first run abw-ask op falcon and wait about 10 min.
Connect > Bastion in the portal will not connect.
The VM stops itself at 03:00 Central, so it may be deallocated. Or another Bastion
Developer session is open (one at a time).
Run Start-JumpBox.bat (about 1 min), close the other session and retry. jumpbox.ps1 -Status shows the state.
What to notice
- A failure at one wall does not open the next: each wall decides again on its own. The data plane
checks the user's own token, so a compromised server reaches no more than the person could, apart
from what its UAMI holds.
- The soft spots are time and preview effects: the guardrail, the 45-90 s kill switch, token lifetime, log lag
and the unlocked audit store. The private MCP server sits outside the gateway kill switch and rate
limit.
- Read the table from the symptom. Every row names the log or the portal page that explains it.
The boundaries, in order (numbers on the path)
1. Callers hold Entra tokens: T1 for Foundry, T2a for an MCP API.
2. Entra signs them and decides the roles inside.
3. Foundry (Wall 0) offers only allowed_tools, holds the user's T2b and screens the turn.
4. APIM (Wall 1) validates T2a or T2b, the role, the client and the rate.
5. The MCP server (Wall 2) re-verifies it and swaps it (OBO, with its T3 assertion) for the
user's T4a/b/c.
6. The data plane (Wall 3) checks its own roles on T4a/b/c.
